source_profile: Aggregated panel signal across Shark Tank - Boomers (2026-08-26), triangulated with cross-file 65-and-older cuts and public Pew / Nielsen / AARP research.
one_line: US adults 61 to 79. Retirement-and-legacy decade. Cable news anchor loyalists, cruise-and-Viking-River travelers, Costco and QVC shoppers, AARP members, church-and-community-rooted, easy-listening and classic-rock, Hallmark and Great American Family, Fidelity and Edward Jones, medical-alert-and-CareCredit readers, aging-parent-of-adult-child role, grandparent identity.

demographics.age_range: 61 to 79. Density in 65-or-older (idx 432) with a strong 55-64 tail (idx 132). Younger buckets fall below 6.
demographics.gender_skew: Roughly 50 male / 48 female. Non-binary and trans identifiers present at low share. Read as gender-binary; slight female pull on wellness, faith, cooking, crafts; slight male pull on classic-cars, motorsports, sports.
demographics.income_band: $100K-plus bands sit near index 96-97 (peak-earning behind them, but retirement assets are substantial). LESS THAN $25K over-indexes at 134 (fixed-income retirees on Social Security). Read as a two-mode distribution: comfortable-retirement homeowners plus fixed-income retirees.
demographics.education: Some College / Associate 123, Bachelors 107, Graduate 106, HS or less 80. Mixed college and trade generation, slightly college-tilted.
demographics.occupation_skew: Read as retired-or-semi-retired (OTHER category over-indexes massively). Among still-working: management / business / professional 43, healthcare 33, skilled trades 71 (older tradespeople staying on).
demographics.ethnicity_skew: White 125, Black 88, Asian 72, Hispanic 61. Read as heaviest majority-white generation, meaningfully less diverse than any younger cohort.
demographics.life_stage: Married 163, Divorced or Separated 146, Single 24, In a relationship 27. Has children over 18 idx 181 (grandparent decade). Empty-nest homeowners, sandwich-generation-caregiver-for-parents-flipping-to-cared-for-self, widowed emerging late-Boomer.

DROP most short-form video-and-drama content (DramaBox, GoodShort, ReelShort vertical shorts).

TIE-BREAK when unsure: does this touch retirement / legacy money, prestige slower-burn TV, full-season sports fandom, cable-news anchor drama, cruises / mid-luxury travel, faith / community / church, aging-in-place tech, grandparent identity, or a Boomer-coded talent? If yes, lean KEEP. If it reads as content aimed at their grandkid or their college-age relative, lean DROP.
expected_kept_share_per_tab: 25-45% of items per tab. Prestige slower-burn TV and classic music should retain a healthy share. Podcasts skew narrower than Gen X (a lot of Millennial / Gen Z-first pods fall out). BookTok drags Books lower. Games narrows the hardest because most gaming culture is younger-first. Headlines and Searches keep a healthy share because cable-news anchor content, retirement news, and Medicare stories all pass.
